angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 695,700 km at 21.33 pc = 0.44 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 46.8742 +/- 0.0270 mas (same row, RUWE 1.03): 21.33 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 1 solar radii from Takeda et al. (2007), ApJS 168, 297, as listed by Willamo et al. (2022), Table 2 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.06729): 695,700 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.942 (0.901 to 0.982) from Gaia DR3 FLAME (Creevey et al. 2023, A&A 674, A26; astrophysical_parameters of the same source); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5837 K from Valenti & Fischer (2005), ApJS 159, 141, as listed by Willamo et al. (2022), Table 2 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.06729). Spin inclination 65 degrees and rotation period 7.676 d from Willamo et al. (2022), Table 2, the values of the ZDI inversion (https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.06729). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Valenti & Fischer (2005), ApJS 159, 141, as listed by Willamo et al. (2022), Table 2 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.06729)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/be-ceti.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.412, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from a blackbody at the star's published temperature (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
